about.title: Orange Cove Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Orange Cove is a small, tight-knit Fresno County community, but that doesn't mean its roads are free of collisions. Public crash records show recurring activity along Hills Valley Road, Anchor Avenue, American Avenue, and Serna Avenue, with reports clustering on Monday mornings between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. — often tied to work commutes and agricultural traffic. Whether you were hit at an intersection, rear-ended in slow traffic, or sideswiped merging onto a busy corridor, the aftermath can be disorienting: medical appointments, missed work, and calls from insurance adjusters all at once. We handle car accident claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Our goal is simple: review what happened and explain your options, without adding pressure or cost while you're already dealing with enough.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity (like a city road or agency) was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault just adjusts the amount. We can help make sure your percentage of blame isn't overstated by the insurer.

items.title: No Recorded Statement Without Guidance
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly after a crash, and anything you say can be used to minimize your claim. Speaking with us first, and preserving evidence like photos and witness contacts, protects your position before you say a word to the other side.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim after a crash in Orange Cove?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If your crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting information early rather than waiting.

items.question: Were there really no reported injury crashes in Orange Cove in 2020?
items.answer: According to the most recent finalized public crash data, Orange Cove recorded zero injury collisions, zero people injured, and zero traffic deaths in 2020. That doesn't mean crashes don't happen on roads like Anchor Avenue or American Avenue in other years — it simply reflects that one particular reporting period.

items.question: What if the accident happened during the Monday midday traffic pattern?
items.answer: Reported crashes in Orange Cove tend to cluster on Mondays between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m., often near higher-traffic corridors. Timing alone doesn't determine fault, but documenting exactly when and where the crash occurred helps us reconstruct what happened.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation just to have your situation reviewed.
